text:
aja: kicking off a nightly kernel-priority sweep on h100-us-west-2 (candidate pool: mm256_gemm_v2, mm256_gemm_v1, tiny-attn-accel)
matt: nice. is this using the new seqlen bucketing (short/med/long) from last week's perf doc?
sophie: yep — buckets are 8-64, 65-512, 513-2048. routing policy is latency-first for short, cost-first for long. will record picks per bucket.
ci-bot: [ci] started nightly-sweep/2045123456 · harness-runner · status: queued
aja: quick note — KV-cache warmup test included (10 warm requests then measure 500 steps). it's been flaky on AVX512 machines, so limiting this run to h100 only.
aja: attaching sample micro output snippet:
```
# mm256_gemm_v2 @ seqlen=128 (batch=4)
lat p50: 12.3ms
lat p95: 18.9ms
throughput: 2.1k tok/s
baseline (mm256_gemm_v1) p50: 11.1ms (+11%)
```
cheng: that p50 regression on med bucket is worrying. is autotuner picking a different kernel because of memory estimate differences?
aja: autotuner log shows it picked mm256_gemm_v2 in med bucket due to lower peak-memory estimate under our estimator. but microbench indicates actual latency is worse for realistic prompt shapes.
matt: could be estimator mismatch: we're using worst-case KV-populated size in planner, but microbench had only partial KV fill. the heuristics need a smoothing factor.
ryan: can someone post the exact planner config used for this sweep?
sophie: planner config snippet:
```
planner {
  mem_mode: "estimate_peak"
  kv_fill_factor: 0.6
  seqlen_buckets: [64, 512, 2048]
  prefer_low_latency_for: "short"
}
```
matt: try kv_fill_factor 0.85 for med bucket — that'll bias toward the older kernel but avoid the latency regression in real workloads.
aja: re-ran a quick subset with kv_fill_factor=0.85 on same seed, med bucket now picks mm256_gemm_v1 and p50=11.2ms (matches baseline). I'll schedule a targeted canary.
ci-bot: [ci] nightly-sweep/2045123456 · harness-runner · status: running (30/120 jobs)
cheng: parallel question — the autotuner's scoring currently weights 70% latency, 30% memory. maybe increase latency weight for med bucket?
sophie: upstream idea: have per-bucket scoring weights. med bucket = latency:0.85, memory:0.15. short = 0.9/0.1. long = 0.5/0.5.
ryan: logging note: add the raw kernel-call traces to artifact bucket so we can reproduce with perf counters if it pops again.
aja: created ticket INF-8723 for the estimator mismatch and follow-ups. cc @matt @sophie
matt: ack. can we also add a flaky metric (p50_delta vs baseline) in perf CI to auto-fail picks that regress >7% in med/short buckets? currently only p95 used.
sophie: yes, adding p50_delta threshold to gating. will push a change to harness.yaml.
ci-bot: [ci] nightly-sweep/2045123456 · harness-runner · status: completed (passed: 113, failed: 7)
aja: failures are mostly the long-bucket quantized kernels — separate issue (quantization kernel select path). I'm going to open a follow-up sweep limited to quantized variants.
cheng: thanks — good catch on kv fill factor. small patch to planner + new gating should keep production picks stable.
ryan: also recommend a short synthetic workload that mimics partial KV usage to include in the microbench suite.
aja: agreed. adding it to harness tomorrow. thanks team :thumbsup:
